nhl.xg_for.label: Team expected goals for (shot quality created), strength-split and adjusted
nhl.xg_for.mechanism: Expected goals credit the quality and location of shots a team generates, so xGF measures offensive process with far less shooting-luck noise than goals.
nhl.xg_for.rationale: Goals are rare and luck-heavy; xG stabilises much faster and is the best public repeatable measure of offence. Subtle: public xG models omit passing/pre-shot movement and goalie quality, treat all shooters equally, and are biased by rink scorer inconsistency in shot location. Use it split by 5v5 / PP and adjust for opponent and for score effects, since trailing teams inflate volume.
nhl.xg_for.measurement: Per-60 xGF at 5v5 (score-and-venue adjusted) and on PP, as exponentially weighted averages (half-life ~25-40 games) shrunk toward league mean with a prior sized by games played; adjust for opponent by regressing team-game xGF on offence and defence team effects plus home indicator (ridge). Report separate 5v5 and special-teams components rather than one blended number.

nhl.xg_against.label: Team expected goals against (shot suppression quality)
nhl.xg_against.mechanism: Expected goals against measure the quality and quantity of chances a team's skaters allow, independent of whether the goalie happened to stop them.
nhl.xg_against.rationale: Separates defensive process (what the skaters control) from goaltending outcome; critical for totals, team totals and for estimating what shot quality a goalie will face. Subtle: xGA as published is goalie-neutral, so any goalie-specific adjustment must be layered on top, and defensive effects partly reflect personnel (injuries to top pair) that stale season averages hide.
nhl.xg_against.measurement: Per-60 xGA at 5v5 and on PK, score/venue-adjusted, exponentially weighted with opponent adjustment via the same ridge team-effects model as xG for; recompute with lineup-weighted projection (replace absent defencemen with replacement-level impact) for the specific game.

nhl.pace.label: Shot-attempt rate / event pace (combined attempts per 60)
nhl.pace.mechanism: A game's total shot-attempt volume (both teams) sets the number of chances available, which scales shots on goal, saves, and total goals.
nhl.pace.rationale: Pace is a team style trait (system, forecheck, trap) and a matchup trait: two high-event teams exceed the sum of their parts, two trap teams undershoot. Subtle: pace changes with score effects and special-teams time, and is partly a coaching-system effect that moves after coaching changes, so long averages lag.

nhl.special_teams.label: Power-play and penalty-kill efficiency (xG-based) and special-teams matchup
nhl.special_teams.mechanism: Special teams convert penalties into goals at far higher rates than 5v5, so unit quality and opponent PK structure shift team goals and totals.
nhl.special_teams.rationale: The PP xGF/60 of the unit and the PK xGA/60 of the opponent combine multiplicatively with expected PP opportunities. Subtle: raw PP% is dominated by shooting luck and sample size; xG-based rates plus personnel (injury to PP1 quarterback) are far more repeatable. nhl.goalie_start.mechanism: The starting goalie determines the goal-prevention quality of the whole game and defines saves-market eligibility, so which goalie plays shifts goals, totals, winners and saves lines.
nhl.goalie_start.rationale: Starter identity is the single largest in-day information event in NHL pricing. nhl.goalie_quality.label: Goalie quality: goals saved above expected (GSAx), danger-zone save rates, workload-adjusted
nhl.goalie_quality.mechanism: A goalie's ability to save shots beyond what shot quality predicts directly changes goals against and the probability a given shot becomes a goal.
nhl.goalie_quality.rationale: GSAx removes shot-quality noise but is extremely noisy per goalie per season; true talent differences are smaller than they appear and shrinkage is mandatory. nhl.toi.label: Projected time on ice by strength state (EV, PP, PK, late-game)

nhl.finishing.label: Shooting percentage / finishing talent (regressed)

period.mechanism: Period outcomes are small-sample versions of the full-game process with period-specific shapes: first periods are cagier, second periods have long changes, third periods are dominated by score effects and empty-net goals. With ties common (period winner can tie), the distribution is heavily discrete and sensitive to the goalie and the first-minutes deployment.

inputs.why: Period-specific scoring and shot shape for each team.
Chance quality creation per 20 minutes.
Chance suppression per 20 minutes.
Goalie identity drives period goals against; warm-up matters in period one.
Third-period behaviour depends on lead/trail state.
PP chances concentrate in particular periods.

Second-period change dynamics.
Late third-period EN goals matter for third-period totals.
Whether period markets include OT or only regulation periods.

interactions.hypothesis: First-period goals depend on opening deployments and goalie state; interacting opening shift lines with starting goalie quality is more informative than team-level rates.
Third-period totals and winners depend on game-script mixture: probability of being tied or trailing late times pull timing.
Second-period outcomes combine long-change effect with team skating depth and line shuffle tendencies.

first_event.target: Which team scores first, whether a goal is scored within the first N minutes, or related first-event contracts.
first_event.mechanism: Time to first goal is governed by the combined scoring hazard of both teams during the opening minutes, modulated by opening lines, early power plays and goalie quality; the first-scorer team is a race between two hazards, tilted by home ice and goalie/skater quality, with a first-period PP draw as a major random factor.

Team chance creation drives hazard.
Opponent suppression reduces hazard.
Goalie quality changes early goals against.

Pace and penalty tendencies interact: fast games with high early penalty rates produce early goals via PP.

player_points.target: Player goals, assists or points (thresholds like 1+ or 2+ points) in a game, with possible void on DNP.
player_points.mechanism: Points are rare events driven by the number of chances a player is on the ice for (TOI by strength state), the shooter/passer role on those chances (PP unit slot, linemates), the quality of those chances (xG), conversion luck, and the opponent's goal prevention including the starting goalie. Distribution is highly discrete and overdispersed, with most mass at 0 and a thin tail, so role and TOI information and regression of luck dominate.

Linemates define who converts passes and shoots.
Shot-quality-based scoring baseline for goals.
Individual shot volume for goal probability.

Opposing goalie quality affects conversion rates.

player_shots.target: Player shots on goal in a game (threshold ladder), settled on official SOG counts.
player_shots.mechanism: SOG = TOI by strength state x attempts per minute x share of attempts reaching the net. Role (D vs F, PP slot, shooting-first players), game script (score effects), opponent block/suppression and rink counting bias determine the mean; variance is high because both TOI and shot rate fluctuate, and thresholds at 2-4 SOG fall in the dense part of the distribution.

goalie_saves.target: Goalie saves in a game (threshold ladder), requiring the goalie to play, settled on official save counts.
goalie_saves.mechanism: Saves = shots on goal faced minus goals allowed. Shots faced are determined by the opponent's attempts and SOG rates against this defence, with score-state effects (trailing team shoots more); goals allowed lower saves slightly. player_other.target: Head-to-head player comparisons (who records more points/shots) and other non-standard player markets.
player_other.mechanism: A head-to-head comparison is the difference of two correlated count processes: each player's expected output given role and matchup, with correlation from shared game environment (both on the same team or opposing teams) and tie handling defined by the rule. The distribution of the difference is wider than either marginal alone and tie/push rules matter.

combo.target: Multi-leg parlay/combo contracts across game outcome and player/team stats in one or more games.
combo.mechanism: A combo's probability is the joint probability of its legs, not the product of marginals: legs share latent drivers (pace, script, goalie, injuries) so correlation can be strongly positive (team win and player points) or negative. Pricing quality depends on marginal accuracy plus a correct joint structure.

season_outcome.target: Season-level outcomes: championship, conference/division titles, playoff qualification, playoff series winners.
season_outcome.mechanism: These markets integrate team strength over many games or a short series: probability is the result of a simulation using team ratings with their uncertainty, injuries, schedule, tiebreakers and bracket structure. Futures are heavily influenced by rating uncertainty and by information that arrives slowly (injuries, trades), and hold time of capital matters.

season_stat.target: Season-total or leader outcomes for players or teams (goals, points, saves, wins), settled at end of season or on specified date.

off_field.target: Non-game events (trades, coaching, league announcements, business or non-hockey questions) settled by public announcement.

player_points_goals_assists.label: Skater goals / assists / points thresholds
player_points_goals_assists.target: Whether a skater records at least k goals, assists or points in the game (typically 1+, 2+, 3+), subject to the contract's DNP rule.
player_points_goals_assists.mechanism: Each goal is a Bernoulli outcome on every shot, so goals follow from shots x shot quality x finishing x opposing goalie; assists require being the passer on a teammate goal and so depend on linemates' finishing and on the player's playmaking role. Points are the union, so volume (TOI, especially PP1 time) dominates, while on-ice shooting luck is noise. The distribution is zero-heavy with thin tails, so thresholds above 1 need joint information on game total and team goals.

Strips lucky/unlucky on-ice shooting%; regress to xG-implied value.

goalie_saves.target: Whether a goalie records at least k saves; eligibility conditional on the goalie playing per the wording.

Goalie quality only matters at the margin (a few shots), while volume matters most. The largest tail risks are an early pull (truncating saves) and goalie identity uncertainty before confirmation; overtime adds shots if included.

The edge from public information is small because lines are efficient; value arises from fast reaction to goalie/lineup news and rule-structure differences across contracts.

Totals are the sum of two overdispersed counts with mild positive correlation through pace, officiating and style; team totals are single-team versions with goalie and opposing defence dominating. period_markets.label: Period winner, total, spread and both-teams-to-score

BTTS: P(team scores >=1) depends on goalie quality of the opponent and own xG; strong-goalie, low-pace games have a materially higher shutout chance than independent Poisson suggests.
First goal: the race between hazards depends on early PP draws and starting lines; interacting penalties and opening deployment shifts the first-team probability.
Season type changes the contract structure: playoffs remove the shootout and add multi-OT events, so the playoff flag interacts with OT scoring rates.

season_futures.label: Championship, division/conference and playoff series futures
season_futures.target: Team wins the Cup, a conference/division, qualifies, or wins a playoff series.
season_futures.mechanism: Futures probabilities come from simulating the remaining schedule/bracket with team strength distributions: game win probabilities from xG-based ratings adjusted for goaltending and injuries, aggregated through the playoff format. Short series amplify goalie variance and injuries, while long-horizon markets are dominated by rating uncertainty and the information arrival rate (trades, injuries). Settlement rules (tiebreakers, bracket structure) matter in close races.

inputs.why: Team strength distribution for simulation.
Offensive process in the rating.
Defensive process in the rating.
Largest single-player driver, especially in the playoffs.
Long-term injuries to key skaters/goalies.
Regression of lucky standings.
Remaining schedule and home/away split alter expected points toward qualification.
Seeding ties resolve by regulation wins and other rules that the simulation must replicate.
Current series score, home pattern and rest feed per-game probabilities for series prices.
Playoff environment parameters.
Trades and coaching changes shift strength after ratings were fitted and market reacts first.
Sportsbook futures prices are the benchmark against which model probabilities are compared.
Time series of probability to infer news reaction.
Points and playoff markets are tails of an 82-game simulation with overtime-point rules and injury uncertainty.

interactions.hypothesis: Short series amplify variance: the same rating gap yields different series win probabilities depending on goalie quality variance and injuries, so goalie uncertainty interacts with series length.
Regress standings luck before simulation but apply NHL tie-break rules to the simulated points to get seeding right.
A long-term injury changes both rating and its uncertainty; the effect on a championship price compounds across rounds.

season_awards_and_stats.label: Season awards and season player stat leaders
season_awards_and_stats.target: Winners of league awards (Hart, Vezina, Norris, Calder, etc.) or leaders/totals for season player stats.
season_awards_and_stats.mechanism: For stat markets, the outcome is rate x opportunity accumulated through the end of the season with health risk, so rest-of-season projection and competitor distribution matter. For awards, voters respond to production, team success and narrative under a specific electorate and ballot timing; a historical voter model with finalist announcements as information events is the natural structure. Both are slow, low-frequency markets where small information steps move prices.

inputs.why: To-date production and projection.
Voter pool and ballot timing determine what information can influence the award result.
A stable or rising role sustains per-game production for the rest of the season.
PP role is a stable driver of points that survives regression better than finishing.
Underlying chance quality for regression.
Finishing above skill regresses, so hot leaders should be discounted for rest-of-season projections.
Goalie awards and saves/wins leaderboards depend on goaltender quality and team defence.
Age and development priors anchor rest-of-season rate and the award narrative.
Games remaining depend on health; late injuries can end an award or leader race.
Team success correlates with award voting and with player opportunity.
Finalist and ballot dates decide when new information stops affecting the result.
Narrative-driving events can change voter preferences between close candidates.
Season totals are sums of over-dispersed per-game counts.

interactions.hypothesis: Projected stat total = rest-of-season rate x games remaining x health: PP role and TOI trend determine the rate, while injury hazard determines games.
Award probability = production rank x team rank x narrative under ballot rules; finalists and ballot deadlines create step changes.
Hot finishing mean-reverts: a leader whose goals exceed ixG is likelier to slide, which interacts with the remaining schedule.

player_h2h.label: Player head-to-head comparisons
player_h2h.target: Whether player A records more of a stat (points, shots, saves) than player B, with tie and DNP rules per the contract.
player_h2h.mechanism: The outcome is the sign of the difference of two correlated count variables. Expected values come from the single-player models (TOI, rates, role, opponent), correlation comes from the shared game environment (same team: script, goalie; opponents: opposing script), and ties are common for small counts so tie handling heavily influences prices. Lineup news on either player can void or flip the comparison.

inputs.why: Minutes of each player by state.
Per-60 shot rates are the base for comparing two players on shots on goal.
Chance quality for points/goals comparisons.
Difference in PP roles gives one player a large share of the high-yield minutes.
Linemate and deployment differences.
Players face different opponents or positions; the matchup difference shifts the expected gap.
Opposing goalie for each player.
Correlation between the two players' counts.
Distribution for tie probability.
Either player's lineup news (linemate absence, injury) shifts the comparison.
The contract may void or settle on a scratched player, which changes the effective probability.
Tie handling and DNP treatment decide who wins ties, which are common for small counts.
Trailing teams shoot more; leading teams protect leads, shifting both players' volume.

interactions.hypothesis: Teammate comparisons: shared game script and linemates mean correlation reduces difference variance; opposing players have different correlation sign via script.
Tie probability matters for small-count stats: with discrete means small, P(tie) can be large; the rules decide who wins ties.
PP roles: the comparison hinges on who gets PP minutes, so penalty expectation interacts with each player's PP slot.

parlay_combo.label: Parlay / combo contracts
parlay_combo.target: Joint outcome of multiple legs (team results, totals, player stats) in one contract.
parlay_combo.mechanism: The contract price must equal the joint probability, which depends on marginal accuracy of each leg and on common latent drivers: game pace, script, goalie quality shocks and lineup changes. Positive correlations (team win and own player's points) make the joint probability exceed the product of marginals, negative correlations the opposite, and leg-void rules change the effective payoff. Modelling this requires a game-level simulation that generates all legs from shared latent variables.

inputs.why: Empirical and simulated correlation between legs.
Marginal distributions per leg.
Latent game script shared across legs.
Team and total goals correlation.
A goalie change shifts opposing scoring, totals and win legs in a correlated manner.
A late scratch changes several legs simultaneously, so lineup state is a shared latent factor.
Team scoring level for the goal-related legs.
Opponent scoring drives the totals and win legs in the opposite direction from own scoring.
Player volume for player legs.
Each leg's settlement and whether a voided leg reduces the combo changes the payoff structure.
Leg-level prices in the ladder must be consistent before combining; inconsistent legs give spurious edge.

interactions.hypothesis: Team win x player points: the correlation is via team goals; conditioning on total expectation and the player's PP share sets the joint uplift over independence.
Goalie shock moves all legs in the same direction (opposing scoring, totals, win legs); correlated shocks need a latent goalie-quality variable.
Script-based negative correlation: favourite wins by large margins reduce its stars' late shots, so a win leg and a shots leg are less correlated than assumed.

offfield_markets.label: Non-hockey and office/personnel markets
offfield_markets.target: Event in the league or organization outside the game (transactions, announcements, business questions).
offfield_markets.mechanism: These markets are driven by organizational decisions and news flow, not on-ice performance; there is little statistical structure and the best-supported hypotheses are reference-class base rates, calendar constraints (deadlines, draft, free agency) and insider-report timing relative to the stated resolution source. Many of these markets are effectively unpredictable from sports data and should be treated as novelty markets.

inputs.why: Reference-class frequency is the prior for novelty markets with no statistical model.
Fixed league dates bound when events can occur and concentrate hazard near them.
Insider reporting and official announcements.
Resolution source and wording.
Price reaction after reports shows how much information the market assigned to the news.
Thin volume means quoted prices are noisy, which limits any inference from them.
Close time relative to the event date defines how much of the hazard is inside the window.
Other venues' prices on the same event provide a cross-check when they exist.
Historical realized frequency for this market type provides a calibration check on listed strikes.

interactions.hypothesis: Base rate x time remaining: hazard rises toward deadline dates, so reference-class frequency must be time-conditioned.
Insider report to official announcement: price after reports measures their credibility and the rules decide what counts.
Thin liquidity makes quotes noisy; volume interacts with price moves to separate information from noise.

team_and_player_season_counting.label: NHL season point/goal totals and counting leaders
team_and_player_season_counting.target: A player's season total (goals, points) or team points relative to a threshold.
team_and_player_season_counting.mechanism: Season totals are games played times per-game rates, where rates depend on ice time, power-play role, linemates and shot quality, and games played depend on injury hazard. Over-dispersion and age curves matter; early-season to-date totals are weak evidence relative to talent priors.

inputs.why: Count distributions over a season.
Time on ice by strength state.
Power-play unit role multiplies even-strength ice time into points; PP1 players earn a large share of their totals there.
Individual expected goals rate.
Finishing talent versus luck: shrunk shooting percentage predicts goals better than raw totals over a season.
Line combinations determine linemates and ice time, so a promotion or demotion shifts the whole scoring rate.
Playing with elite centres or wingers raises assist and goal rates independent of the player's own talent.
Age curves set the expected change in rate from last season: young players rise and veterans decline on average.
Shot-attempt rate per 60 is the most stable component of goal scoring and anchors the projection.

interactions.hypothesis: Power-play share multiplies even-strength time on ice into points.
Expected goals with shrunk finishing talent beats raw goals for season totals.
Age declines show first in ice time, then production.
